post.description:
Requires breeding.create. The workflow must be supported by the species capabilities of the cycle's species
(incubation -> supports_incubation, pregnancy -> supports_pregnancy, both need supports_breeding), else 422 on workflow.
The biological reference is frozen on the project. Expectation: an exact reference gives expectation.type=exact
(start + days); a ranged reference gives expectation.type=window (start + min .. start + max, never a midpoint);
a species without a numeric reference, or whose reference_config sets automatic_expectation=false (e.g. honeybee, caste-dependent), gets type=none unless a
manual expected_date / expected_from+expected_to is supplied. Nothing here changes population.
Closed cycles are rejected (409 cycle_closed). The required idempotency_key is farm-wide: an identical retry returns the
original project (201), a changed payload is 409.

Incubation with `consume_egg_stock: true` also takes `eggs_set` eggs out of the farm's available egg stock in the same transaction (needs inventory.use):
one stock-out (reason incubation) linked to the project and its cycle, from `egg_storage_location_id` (optional when the farm has one active store).
Too few eggs is 409 insufficient_stock and nothing - project included - is written. Omit the flag to leave stock untouched. `egg_stock` on the project
is derived from its stock movements.

**Requires farm permission:** `breeding.create`.

The frontend obtains a Google Identity Services ID token (`credential`) and posts it here.
The backend verifies the token's signature, issuer, audience and expiry with Google's keys,
then finds/links/creates the local user. Google-verified emails are marked verified and NO

`422` (no verified Google email), `429`, `503 google_unavailable`.

post.description:
Requires record.create; population_adjustment additionally record.adjust, correction links record.reverse.
See /record-types/{type}/schema for strictly allowed details; unknown detail keys fail 422.
recorded_at requires an explicit offset, cycle start <= event <= now. Closed cycles reject new records.
Required idempotency_key is farm-wide: exact validated payload replay returns the original record (201), changed payload 409.
Measurements use Phase 5 components/context; feed_use and the Phase 13 crop types (fertilizer, pesticide, planting, harvest) may link stock via details.inventory (see Phase 9 and Phase 13).
feed_use with details.inventory is the one entry for "feed used for livestock": it writes the record and the stock-out (reason production_use) together.
egg_collection and milk (eggs / milk produced by this cycle's livestock) ALWAYS add the quantity to the farm's own Eggs / Milk stock in the same transaction
(stock-in reason production, linked to the record and cycle; needs inventory.use). The item and, on a farm with no store, a "Main Store" are created on first use.
details.inventory.storage_location_id optionally picks the store (required when several are active, 422). Packages (crate...) resolve through details.context
if given, else through the Eggs / Milk item's own conversions. A zero quantity records production but moves no stock. Reversing the record compensates the stock
(409 insufficient_stock while those eggs / milk have since left). Donated, purchased or received eggs and milk are never records: use POST /inventory/stock-in with `output`.

**Requires farm permission:** `record.create`.

post.description:
Defines what a package holds in a context. A context is always chosen by `context_type` + `context_id`: a crop
(`crop_type` + an id from `GET /master/crops`, e.g. Maize) or one of this farm's own measurement contexts
(`custom` + an id from `GET /settings/measurement-contexts`, e.g. "Feed Grower Mash", "Eggs"; create it first with
`POST /settings/measurement-contexts`). The id must resolve to an active crop or an active context of this farm,
otherwise `422` on `context_id`. `package_unit` is a `package` unit code (bag, crate, ...);
`target_unit` is a weight, volume, area or count unit code; `quantity_per_package` is an exact decimal above
zero (up to 12 digits + 6 decimals; whole when the target is a count such as `piece`). So Feed and Maize can
both have a `bag` with different contents. The farm comes from your session, never the body. Requires
`measurement.manage`.

Errors: `403`, `409 conversion_exists` (details: existing_id, is_active), `422` validation,
`422 invalid_conversion_ratio`, `422 unknown_unit`, `422 unit_not_selectable`, `422 unit_dimension_mismatch`,
`422 incompatible_units` (a package cannot contain a package), `429`.

**Requires farm permission:** `measurement.manage`.

change - create another definition instead (rename a context with `PATCH /settings/measurement-contexts/{id}`). A change to quantity, target
or active state increases `version`. Past normalized quantities are NOT affected: each keeps its own snapshot of
the definition it used. A deactivated definition stops resolving for new entries. Other farms' ids are `404`.
Requires `measurement.manage`.

Errors: `403`, `404`, `422` validation, `422 invalid_conversion_ratio`, `422 unit_not_selectable`, `429`.

**Requires farm permission:** `measurement.manage`.

post.description:
Send the parts the user typed as `components` (`[{"quantity": "3", "unit": "crate"}, {"quantity": "14",
"unit": "piece"}]`) and, whenever a package unit (bag, crate, ...) is used, the `context`
(`{"type": "custom", "id": "<uuid>"}` - the `context.type`/`context.id` of a package conversion; the id must be
a crop type or one of this farm's active measurement contexts, else `422` on `context.id`). Optional
`result_unit` chooses the unit of `total`.

Result: `entered` (preserved as typed), `normalized` (the total in the dimension's canonical unit - what to
store), `total` (the same in `result_unit`, else the package's target unit, else the first part's unit) and
`snapshot` (a self-contained record of every conversion used; store it with the record so later changes to
farm settings never change history). Example: 3 crates + 14 pieces with 1 crate = 30 pieces -> total
`104 piece`. Only this farm's active definitions are used, and the API never guesses a context.

Errors: `403`, `422` validation, `422 incompatible_units` (details: from_unit, to_unit, dimensions),
`422 conversion_context_required` / `422 ambiguous_conversion` (details: candidates),
`422 conversion_not_configured` (details: unit, context), `422 invalid_quantity` (details: unit, reason),
`422 unknown_unit`, `422 unit_not_selectable`, `429`.

**Requires farm permission:** `measurement.view`.

Requires sale.create; a correction (corrects_sale_id) additionally needs sale.cancel, and the optional invoice block
("Save & Create Invoice") needs invoice.create. One transaction creates the sale and its lines, ONE Phase 9 stock-out
(reason sale, linked to the line) per stock line - produce only, quantities in the Phase 5 components format, packages
resolved through the item's own conversion - and ONE population-ledger exit (a livestock_sale record with a negative
population_delta, linked to the line) per livestock line. other lines have no physical effect. A sale books NO income and
creates NO invoice by itself: income is booked when a payment is received. Amounts are strings with at most two decimals;
the total is the exact sum of the line amounts. Any failure (409 insufficient_stock / insufficient_population / lot_expired /
item_inactive / cycle_closed, 404 foreign ids) rolls everything back. The required idempotency_key is farm-wide: an
identical retry returns the original (201) with no second stock-out, population exit or invoice; a changed payload is 409.

**Requires farm permission:** `sale.create`.

apiKey.description: Sanctum session cookie set by /auth/login, /auth/register or /auth/google. Send requests with credentials and, for POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE, the X-XSRF-TOKEN header (see docs/api/README.md).

email.description: Email of an existing, verified account.

farms.description:
Every farm the user ACTIVELY belongs to (oldest membership first, the same order the default farm is chosen by). Send a farm's `id` as the
`X-Farm-Id` header to work in it; permissions are never listed here - they come from GET /farm → membership.permissions for the selected farm.

marketplace.description:
Marketplace participation, independent of farms. `shop_count` = shops the user is a member of (any status); drive the seller area from
GET /marketplace/my/shops. A user can have farms, shops, both or neither.

outcome_date.description: Actual outcome day (farm-local). Separate from the expected date/window and from created_at.

operational_record_id.description: The Phase 8 operational record carrying the population effect (or its compensation); null when live_count is 0.

eggs_set.description: Incubation only; null otherwise. Eggs set are not live population.

expectation.description:
Operational expectation: an exact date OR a window, never both. source: reference (derived from the snapshot), manual, or none.
When type is none, no_expectation_reason says why (no_numeric_reference, qualified_reference: reference_config.automatic_expectation=false) or null when simply not provided.

biological_reference.description: Biological reference frozen when the project started (later master-data edits never change it).

egg_stock.description:
Eggs this project took from available stock (incubation workflow with consume_egg_stock), derived from its stock movements.
null when it never touched stock. returned counts only eggs the farmer explicitly sent back; net_out is what is still counted as in incubation.

outcomes.description: Outcome rows including reversals, oldest first.

result.description: The current actual outcome (not reversed), with expected-vs-actual variance; null while none.

BreedingStatus.description: active -> completed (an outcome exists) | cancelled (abandoned); reversing the only outcome returns completed -> active.

BreedingWorkflow.description: The two reproductive modes, each unlocked by a species capability (never by comparing species names).
BreedingWorkflow.title: BreedingWorkflow

eggs_returned_to_stock.description: How many eggs go back to available stock. Omit = nothing returns (the eggs are not assumed usable). At most what the project took and has not returned. Needs inventory.use.

egg_storage_location_id.description: Store the returned eggs go to; defaults to the store they were taken from.

recorded_at.description: When the goods were returned / the purchase was voided (explicit offset); the stock reversal is dated here.
When the goods/animals came back (explicit offset); the stock and population compensation is dated here.

interval.description: Used for a paid plan (default monthly); ignored for the default plan.

reason.description: Why support is changing this farm's plan (kept in the audit trail).

completed_at.description: When the work was finished (UTC ISO-8601, not in the future). Defaults to now.

evidence.description: An ALREADY SAVED actual record to link. Completing never creates one. Required when the task requires evidence.

ConversionContextType.description: What a package conversion is about. The context is what makes "1 bag = ? kg" answerable: a bag of maize and a bag of feed differ. Stored as a (type, id) pair - the id always identifies a real, validated entity, never display text - so later phases can add their own types (for example `inventory_item`, id = the item's UUID) without a schema change.

name.description: Only farm name is collected; country/currency/timezone/language use platform defaults.

filters.description: The same filters the report accepts. Omitted dates are defaulted when the export is requested, and the resolved filters are stored on the export.

idempotency_key.description: Required. Retrying the same request returns the same export; reusing the key with different content is a 409.

DueState.description: Presentation state derived from status + due date; never persisted.
DueState.title: DueState

cancel_future_tasks.description: Also cancel the schedule's open future tasks (due after today). Completed and past tasks are kept.

EvidenceType.description: The kinds of actual record that can evidence a completed task. The task never creates one.
EvidenceType.title: EvidenceType

membership.description: What the CALLER may do on this farm; drive UI visibility from this, backend still enforces.

is_system.description: True for platform categories shared by every farm.

amount.description: Always positive; a reversal row offsets the original in every total.

credential.description: Google Identity Services ID token (JWT) obtained by the frontend.

mortality_record_id.description: The linked Phase 8 mortality record, if any. Population is only ever changed by that record.

stock.description: Derived from movements and never writable. `quantity` is in the item's stock_unit; `normalized` is the canonical unit (g, ml or the count unit).

reason_label.description: Human label of reason (e.g. "Put into incubation"); null when the movement has no reason.

quantity_delta.description: Signed change in the canonical unit (positive = stock added).

measurement.description: Entered parts, normalised totals and the replayable Phase 5 conversion snapshot.

production_cycle_id.description: Production cycle and breeding project this movement belongs to (record-driven and incubation movements); null otherwise.

source.description: The domain event that explains this movement, so history reads as events rather than numbers.

customer.description: Snapshot taken when the invoice was issued; later contact edits never change it.

sale_id.description: The sale to invoice. Required on POST /invoices; taken from the URL on POST /sales/{sale}/invoice.

issue_date.description: Farm-local day; defaults to today, never before the sale or in the future.

LivestockGroup.description: Product grouping of livestock species for selectors and forms (a presentation/product classification only: it never drives biological behaviour, which comes from species capabilities). Fish/aquaculture species have no group.
LivestockGroup.title: LivestockGroup

is_system_managed.description: true for the farm's automatic Eggs / Milk output items (resolved by the system, `output: eggs|milk`); they cannot be mistaken for a farmer-defined item by name.

stock.description: Derived from movements and never writable. `quantity` is in the item's stock_unit; `normalized` is the canonical unit (g, ml or the count unit).

type.description: A notification type code; GET /notification-preferences lists the codes available to you.

source.description: What it is about, to open it: a production cycle, inventory item, task, export, ... (null for farm-wide conditions).

data.description: Why it was raised (rule, measured values, thresholds) for insight-based notifications.

OperationCategory.description: Fundamental production behaviour of an operation type.
OperationCategory.title: OperationCategory

channels.description: Channel switches. Omitted channels keep their value.

types.description: Per-type switches ({type_code: bool}); only the types GET /notification-preferences lists for you are accepted.

amount.description: Always positive; a reversal row offsets the original in the invoice balance.

finance_transaction_id.description: The ONE income entry this payment booked in the finance ledger (for a reversal: the offsetting ledger row).

available_record_types.description:
Detail only. The record types POST /records accepts for this cycle right now: the same cycle-kind, species-capability and open-cycle rules the
create endpoint applies (a closed cycle accepts none). Not filtered by the member's permissions - match `permissions_required` against GET /farm → membership.permissions.

finance_transaction_id.description: The one expense this purchase booked (null when none was booked), and the entry that offsets it after a cancellation.

value.description: Shape depends on the setting key and is validated against that setting's own rule.

amount.description: Money actually received, in the farm currency, a string with at most two decimals; may not exceed the invoice balance.

received_on.description: Farm-local day the money was received; not in the future.

recorded_at.description: When it was entered (explicit offset); defaults to now. Kept separate from created_at.

finance_category_id.description: Income category for the ledger entry; defaults to the sale category.

Recurrence.description: none = a single task; daily = every N days; weekly = every N weeks on the chosen ISO weekdays.
Recurrence.title: Recurrence

filters.description: The exact resolved filters the file is produced with (omitted dates were defaulted when the export was requested).

download_path.description: Present once the export is completed and not expired: GET this path (authenticated) to download the file.

recorded_at.description: When the money was returned/voided (explicit offset); defaults to now.

occurred_on.description: Farm-local day of the reversal (between the original day and today); defaults to today.

payment_status.description:
Receivable state, derived from the live invoice: uninvoiced (no invoice), unpaid, partially_paid, paid. A sale is not paid
or unpaid by itself - only its invoice is. amount_paid / outstanding are null while uninvoiced.

reference_config.description: Allowed keys depend on the capability (see GET /platform-admin/master/capabilities); null or an empty object clears it.

features.description: Keys are Feature registry values, for example `advanced_reports`.

limit.description: Either a number, or `unlimited: true` with no number.

reason.description: Shown to the seller and kept in the audit trail.

ShopStatus.description: Publishing lifecycle of a seller shop. Only `active` shops are visible to the public.
ShopStatus.title: ShopStatus

decision.description: verified | rejected (from a pending request) | unverified (revokes the badge)

ShopVerificationStatus.description: Trust badge, independent of the publishing lifecycle: an active shop may be unverified.
ShopVerificationStatus.title: ShopVerificationStatus

StockInReason.description:
Stable, domain-level reasons for stock coming IN. The manual endpoint accepts every case except the system-only ones; purchases (Phase 14) book their own "purchase" stock-in with a source link and expense, crop harvests / egg collections / milk records book their own stock-in through the operational record that explains it. | | |---| | `opening_balance`
| | `purchase`
| | `donation`
| | `aid`
| | `received`
| | `production`
Produced on the farm. Manual only for stock no record explains (e.g. home-mixed feed); produce comes from its record. | | `returned`
Eggs handed back to stock when an incubation is cancelled or reduced. Written only by the breeding workflow. | | `other`
|
StockInReason.title: StockInReason

inventory_item_id.description: The item receiving stock. Omit when `output` is used.

output.description: eggs | milk: the farm's own egg / milk stock (created automatically on first use), so no item has to be set up. For stock that was NOT produced on this farm (purchase, donation, received, opening balance, other); produced-on-farm eggs and milk are recorded with POST /records.

storage_location_id.description: Required, except with `output`: then the only active storage location is used, a farm with none gets a "Main Store", and several active locations need a choice (422).

lot_id.description: Existing lot of this item. Use `lot` instead to receive into a (new or existing) lot by code.

lot.description: Lot code (and expiry for expiry-tracked items). An existing code of the same item is reused; a different expiry is rejected.

StockOutReason.description: Stable, domain-level reasons for stock going OUT (never channel-specific codes such as "farmers_market": those belong to the sale). `use`, `expired` and `wasted` are kept for existing clients and records. System-only reasons are written by the workflow that owns the real-world event and are refused on POST /inventory/stock-out so one event can never be entered twice: sale -> POST /sales, production_use -> POST /records (feed_use), incubation -> POST /breeding-projects.
StockOutReason.title: StockOutReason

inventory_item_id.description: The item leaving stock. Omit when `output` is used.

output.description: eggs | milk: the farm's own egg / milk stock, so no item id is needed. Sales, incubation and feed use are recorded through their own workflows.

storage_location_id.description: Required, except with `output`: then the only active storage location is used and several active locations need a choice (422).

result.description: Pregnancy: confirmed / not confirmed. Incubation: fertile / not fertile.

fertile_count.description: Incubation only (candling): number of eggs found fertile; at most eggs_set.

live_count.description: Actual live births / hatched chicks. 0 records an unsuccessful attempt and adds nothing; a positive count joins the project's cycle population through the Phase 8 ledger automatically.

loss_count.description: Stillborn / dead-in-shell / infertile; informational. For incubation live + loss cannot exceed eggs_set.

corrects_outcome_id.description: Reversed outcome this one replaces (needs breeding.reverse).

workflow.description: incubation needs the species capability supports_incubation; pregnancy needs supports_pregnancy.

start_date.description: Incubation start / service date (farm-local day), between the cycle start and today.

eggs_set.description: Incubation only (required there, rejected for pregnancy). Eggs set are not live population.

consume_egg_stock.description: Incubation only. true takes eggs_set eggs out of the farm's available egg stock in the same request (stock-out reason incubation, linked to this project). 409 insufficient_stock when too few; needs inventory.use. Omit to leave stock untouched.

egg_storage_location_id.description: Store the eggs are taken from. Optional when the farm has exactly one active storage location; required when it has several.

females_bred.description: Pregnancy only: how many females were bred.

expected_offspring.description: Expected offspring is an estimate and never changes population.

expected_date.description: Optional manual expected date (exact). Provide this OR expected_from + expected_to. Overrides the biological reference without altering its snapshot.

roles.description: One or both of supplier / customer. A contact that is both stays ONE record.

farm_id.description: The farm always comes from the caller's farm context; system flags/codes are never client input.

items.description: Ingredients as percentages of the mix; they must add up to exactly 100. A formula never holds or changes stock.

details.description: Type-specific object; only fields returned by /master/health-record-types are accepted.

mortality_record_id.description: An existing Phase 8 mortality record of the same cycle. Health never creates a mortality event itself.

corrects_record_id.description: Replace a reversed health record once (same type and cycle).

medicines.description: One entry per medicine used. Each consumes linked stock exactly once.

withdrawal_days.description: Overrides the medicine's default withdrawal period. 0 = none.

stock_unit.description: Unit code (kg, g, l, ml, piece, egg, head, planting_unit...). Fixes the item's measurement basis; packages never.

tracks_expiry.description: Expiry tracking requires lot tracking: expiry belongs to a lot.

parent_id.description: Always references a location, never a production area or storage location.

context_id.description: Existence/ownership is checked in PackageConversionService::resolveContext (crop type, or this farm's context).

farm_id.description: The farm always comes from the caller's farm context; a context is chosen by id, never by typing a label here.

slug.description: Stable machine identity; cannot be changed later.
